tldr: Headlines across all six buckets converge on the intra-GOP confirmation fight over Todd Blanche's AG nomination, with the rescission of the 'anti-weaponization fund' as the resolution mechanism. UK outlets alone depart from this transactional frame to foreground critics' claims that the deal is legally hollow and easily reversed.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only outlet to identify Blanche as 'Former Trump personal lawyer' in the headline itself, anchoring the story in political loyalty rather than the institutional confirmation process — a framing absent from every other bucket.

The only outlet to bundle the Blanche fund rescission with a separate Iran story ('Trump calls off striking Iran') in a single headline, collapsing two distinct stories into one title — a newsletter-format choice that dilutes the confirmation-fight frame dominant across all other US outlets.

The only outlet to use the phrase 'Trump slush fund' in the headline, applying a charged characterization that no other outlet — including the Independent — adopted, and foregrounding critics' voices ('Completely hollow') ahead of the factual rescission event.

bottom_line: The headline layer frames the Blanche confirmation as a resolved political deal story — GOP holdouts capitulate, fund is rescinded, vote proceeds — with UK outlets as the only dissenters, whose titles emphasize Democratic and legal-expert doubts about whether the agreement is enforceable.
